'''Sir John Edwin Enderby''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|size=100%|CBE|FRS|FInstP}}<ref name=frs>{{cite web|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20151117020735/https://royalsociety.org/people/john-enderby-11400/ |url=https://royalsociety.org/people/john-enderby-11400/ |title=Sir John Enderby CBE FRS |publisher=[[Royal Society]] |location=London |archivedate=17 November 2015 }} One or more of the preceding sentences incorporates text from the royalsociety.org website where: {{quote|"All text published under the heading 'Biography' on Fellow profile pages is available under [[Creative Commons license|Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License]]." --{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/ |title=Royal Society Terms, conditions and policies |accessdate=2016-03-09 |url-status=live |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150925220834/https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/ |archivedate=2015-09-25 }}}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://royalsocietypublishing.org/doi/10.1098/rsbm.2025.0001|title=Sir John Edwin Enderby. 16 January 1931 — 3 August 2021|last=Evans FRS|first=Robert|date=2025|journal=Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society|last2=Soper FRS|first2=Alan K.}}</ref> (16 January 1931 – 3 August 2021) was a British [[physicist]], and was Professor of Physics at [[University of Bristol]] from 1976 to 1996.<ref>{{cite web|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150512162139/http://www.bristol.ac.uk/pace/graduation/honorary-degrees/hondeg06/enderby.html|archivedate=12 May 2015|url=http://www.bristol.ac.uk/pace/graduation/honorary-degrees/hondeg06/enderby.html|title=Sir John Edwin Enderby|publisher=University of Bristol}}</ref> He developed innovative ways of using neutrons to study matter at the microscopic level. His research has particularly advanced our understanding of the structure of multicomponent liquids— those made up of two or more types of atoms – including commonly used liquid alloys and glasses.<ref name=frs/><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Collins|first1=Kim D.|last2=Neilson|first2=George W.|last3=Enderby|first3=John E.|title=Ions in water: Characterizing the forces that control chemical processes and biological structure|journal=Biophysical Chemistry|volume=128|issue=2–3|year=2007|pages=95–104|issn=0301-4622|doi=10.1016/j.bpc.2007.03.009|pmid=17418479}}</ref>

==Education==
Enderby was educated at Chester Grammar School<ref name=whoswho/> and the [[University of London]] where he was awarded Bachelor of Science and Doctor of Philosophy degrees.<ref name=enderbyphd>{{cite thesis|degree=PhD|publisher=University of London|title=Some electrical properties of liquid metals|first=John Edwin|last=Enderby|year=1963|id={{ProQuest|301234547}}}} {{subscription required}}</ref>

==Career and research==
Enderby’s techniques mean that the relative positions of the various types of atomic nuclei can be deduced from diffraction patterns arising from the quantum wavelike scattering of the neutrons. His work includes the surprise discovery that aqueous solutions — important in biology as the environment for an organism’s chemical reactions — have a quasi-lattice structure.<ref name=frs/>

He was the H.O. Wills Professor of Physics and Head of Department, from 1981 to 1994 and Deputy Director (Directeur-adjoint) of the [[Institut Laue–Langevin]] from 1985 to 1988.

==Personal life==
Enderby died on 3 August 2021, at the age of 90.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Johnston|first1=Hamish|title=Neutron-science pioneer John Enderby dies aged 90 |url=https://physicsworld.com/a/neutron-science-pioneer-john-enderby-dies-aged-90/|website=Physics World|date=6 August 2021}}</ref>

==Awards and honours==
Enderby was awarded the [[Faraday Medal and Prize|Guthrie Medal]] of the [[Institute of Physics]], an institution he later served as President. Enderby was elected a [[List of Fellows of the Royal Society elected in 1985|Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS) in 1985]]<ref name=frs/> and was Physical Secretary and Vice-President of the society from 1999 to 2004<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.vrijmetselaarsgilde.eu/Maconnieke%20Encyclopedie/RMAP~1/TRS/manage.htm|title=Management of the Royal Society}}</ref> and was Chair of the Royal Society's Publishing Board ''ex officio''. He was President of the [[Institute of Physics]] from 2004 to 2006.  Enderby's contributions have been recognised by the award of a [[Order of the British Empire|CBE]] in 1997 and a [[Knight]]hood for services to Science and Technology in 2004.<ref name=whoswho/>
